mainEntity.name: How do Cognito Forms entry limits work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Entries are metered monthly on every tier: 100 a month on the free Individual plan, 2,000 on Pro, 10,000 on Team, and unlimited only on Enterprise at $129 a month billed annually. Annual plans absorb overages through what Cognito calls a usage wallet.

mainEntity.name: Does Cognito Forms charge a fee on payments?

acceptedAnswer.text: On the lower tiers, yes. Taking payments through Stripe carries a Cognito convenience fee of 2% on Individual and 1% on Pro, on top of Stripe's own fees. Team and Enterprise are exempt. Formester adds no platform fee on any plan.

mainEntity.name: Does Cognito Forms have AI and an MCP server?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes to both, which is why this page does not claim an AI gap. Cognito ships prompt-to-form generation that also produces a workflow diagram, and a Cognito Forms MCP Connector for Claude and ChatGPT from the Pro plan upward. Formester's MCP server is on the Business plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I customize how Cognito forms look?

acceptedAnswer.text: Up to a point. Styling exists on the lower tiers, but Cognito's own plan comparison puts Customize Appearance on the Enterprise plan. Limited design flexibility is among the most repeated themes in their Capterra reviews.

The honest read

Why do teams leave Cognito Forms?

Cognito Forms is well liked. What pushes teams off it is usually a ceiling rather than a flaw.

Prices that climbed over time

Price increases are the most repeated complaint in their Capterra reviews, including from non-profits describing even a nominal cost as hard to absorb.

Design flexibility runs out

Four reviewers describe limited design flexibility, no font control, and no way to embed video. Cognito's own plan comparison puts Customize Appearance on Enterprise.

Entries are metered on every tier

The free plan stops at 100 entries a month and Pro at 2,000. One reviewer describes hitting the cap mid-campaign and missing submissions.

Advanced features carry a learning curve

Four reviewers name calculations and multi-layered rules as fiddly to set up, even while praising the logic engine itself.

Honest comparison

When is Cognito Forms still the better choice?

Formester is not the answer for every team. Three cases where Cognito Forms is the better call.

Complex logic has to cost nothing

Conditional logic and calculations sit on Cognito's free tier and are its most praised features.

  • Show and hide fields, branch pages, and route emails conditionally at no cost
  • A full expression language for computed values, defaults, and validation
  • Formester puts conditional logic on the Personal plan at $13 a month

Choose Cognito Forms when heavy logic has to be free

Approvals and client portals are the job

Cognito is built around workflow, not only collection.

  • Workflow tasks, approval routing, and a client portal on Team and above
  • Guest access for external reviewers, five included on Team
  • Formester collects and routes data but does not ship an approval portal

Choose Cognito Forms for approval-driven processes

You handle PHI under HIPAA

Cognito supports HIPAA with a BAA on its Enterprise plan.

  • HIPAA support with a business associate agreement on Enterprise
  • Encryption at rest from the Team plan upward
  • Formester is not HIPAA certified and says so plainly

Choose Cognito Forms when PHI is part of the workflow

Privacy and data ownership

Who owns your form data?

You do. Everything moving through your forms is Customer Data: the prompts you type, the structures the AI drafts, and every response someone submits. Section 4.4 of our Data Processing Addendum bars Formester from using any of it to train AI models, run advertising, or feed analytics and marketing. The Google Gemini integration that drafts forms works inside the same boundary.

Responses travel over TLS, sit encrypted at rest, and payment data carries an extra AES-256 layer through Stripe. Formester is GDPR, UK GDPR, and CCPA compliant. We are not SOC 2, ISO 27001, or HIPAA certified, and the security page says exactly that instead of hinting otherwise. Compensating controls are in place: encryption in transit and at rest, annual third-party penetration testing, enforced 2FA, and encrypted backups.

DPA §4.4 · January 2026
"Formester shall not use Customer Data for purposes of analytics, advertising, marketing, or training of artificial intelligence or machine learning models, except as strictly necessary to provide the Services."

Formester Data Processing Addendum, effective January 2026.
